scope: Selected public-source cyber observations concerning Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia; not an exhaustive incident census or prevalence dataset.
methodology: Each observation captures one bounded claim from a named public authority. Source terminology and attribution confidence are preserved; nearby events are not merged into campaigns without evidence. Europe-context actors are sourced from APT Notes and do not imply Baltic activity unless an explicit observation id is attached.

records.title: Broadcast content replaced in two incidents
records.summary: Lithuania's NCSC reported two incidents affecting online music streams where original playlists were allegedly replaced with recorded disinformation.

records.title: 63% increase in recorded incidents
records.summary: The 2024 CTAC report connected the increase to improved identification and more active reporting; 59% of recorded incidents involved social engineering.

records.title: 2,888 incidents recorded, including 19 major incidents
records.summary: Lithuania's NCSC recorded 19 major incidents, 380 minor incidents and 2,489 near misses in 2025. The lower total than 2024 does not by itself establish lower threat exposure because category and reporting effects matter.

records.title: Phishing remained dominant while fraud reports increased
records.summary: The NCSC recorded 1,551 social-engineering incidents, 49% of the annual total, down from 2,288 in 2024. Illegal activity and fraud increased from 444 to 907 records.

records.title: Foreign intruder presence found during threat hunts
records.summary: CERT.LV analysed more than 140,000 installations in 31 organisations and reported high-confidence foreign intruder presence in eight; the public summary did not name the actors.

records.title: Continued politically motivated DDoS waves
records.summary: CERT.LV described DDoS waves against public authorities and selected sectors as Russia and proxy-hacktivist activity; reported impact was limited.

records.title: 846 incidents and record device visibility
records.summary: CERT.LV processed 846 incidents and identified 757,286 compromised or weakly configured devices. The authority cautioned that expanded SOC visibility contributes to the observed increase.

records.title: DNS firewall blocked more than 2.5 million malicious-site visits
records.summary: CERT.LV reported a 139% quarter-over-quarter increase in DNS firewall blocks and said automated detection blocked 266 fraudulent campaigns before they became incidents.

records.title: 84 DDoS attacks registered in one month
records.summary: RIA reported a then-record monthly total affecting a wider target set that included government, finance, transport and media; most attacks had limited impact.

records.title: Unit 29155 operations jointly attributed
records.summary: Estonia joined a multinational government advisory attributing espionage, sabotage and reputational operations against global targets to Russian GRU Unit 29155.

records.title: Estonia co-sealed Laundry Bear Zimbra advisory
records.summary: Estonia's Foreign Intelligence Service joined a multinational advisory attributing a Zimbra email-collection campaign to Russian state-supported actors primarily tracked as Laundry Bear. The advisory does not report an Estonian victim.
records.sector: Defence, Government, Education, Energy, Law Enforcement, Media, NGOs and Technology

records.title: Record 756 DDoS attacks, fewer than 100 with impact
records.summary: RIA recorded more than one-third growth in DDoS attempts while reporting that fewer than 100 affected target services, indicating improved resilience despite higher volume.

records.title: 1,232 incidents with impact recorded in June
records.summary: RIA reported high-impact DDoS activity, disruptions affecting national digital services and a customer-data breach in a southern Estonian booking system. These were separate events, not one campaign.

records.title: NoName057(16) DDoS campaign targeted Lithuanian airports
records.summary: CERT-EU described a February 2023 DDoS campaign launched against Lithuanian airports. The cited record establishes targeting, not material disruption or a victim count.

records.title: NoName057(16) claimed Latvia's National Defence Academy
records.summary: CERT-EU recorded a NoName057(16) claim against Latvia's National Defence Academy without confirming impact. The Atlas preserves the distinction between an actor claim and an observed incident.

records.title: UNC1151 reporting included Lithuania in regional targeting
records.summary: Mandiant's public assessment included Lithuania in regional targeting associated with UNC1151 and Ghostwriter-linked intrusion activity. This is a targeting-scope record, not an inventory of Lithuanian compromises.
records.sector: Government, Politics, Media and Civil Society

records.title: UNC1151 reporting included Latvia in regional targeting
records.summary: Mandiant's public assessment included Latvia in regional targeting associated with UNC1151 and Ghostwriter-linked intrusion activity. This is a targeting-scope record, not an inventory of Latvian compromises.
records.sector: Government, Politics, Media and Civil Society

records.title: Unit 29155 linked to compromise of Estonian ministries
records.summary: The Council of the European Union recorded unauthorised access to Estonian ministries and theft of confidential documents in 2020 when sanctioning three GRU Unit 29155 officers.
records.attribution: Council of the European Union sanctions record

actor_context_source.name: APT Notes by HECAVEX
actor_context_source.method: Manually selected Europe-relevant actor context from the named reviewed APT Notes release. This layer does not create Baltic attribution; only baltic_observation_ids establishes an Atlas mapping.

actor_context.name: NoName057(16)
actor_context.summary: A pro-Russia DDoS network that recruits participants around an automated attack tool and repeatedly targets Ukraine-supporting governments, public services and critical sectors in Europe.
actor_context.europe_relevance: Reviewed reporting includes direct Lithuanian targeting and a separately labelled claim against a Latvian defence-education institution.

actor_context.name: GRU Unit 29155
actor_context.summary: A Russian military intelligence unit associated with espionage, sabotage, reputational harm and the destructive WhisperGate operation against Ukraine.
actor_context.europe_relevance: Official reporting records an Estonian ministry compromise. The wider Europe context is retained without inferring additional Baltic targets.

actor_context.name: Void Blizzard
actor_context.summary: A Russia-affiliated espionage cluster using commodity credentials, stolen session cookies and cloud-native collection against NATO, EU and Ukraine-related targets.
actor_context.europe_relevance: Estonia's Foreign Intelligence Service co-sealed the Laundry Bear Zimbra advisory, creating a reporting connection without establishing an Estonian victim.

actor_context.name: UAC-0010 / Gamaredon
actor_context.summary: Russian state-sponsored espionage actor associated with FSB Centre 18 and sustained targeting of Ukrainian government and defence organisations.
actor_context.europe_relevance: Ukraine-focused activity and an EU sanctions record make the actor relevant to the wider European threat picture.

actor_context.name: Secret Blizzard
actor_context.summary: Russian espionage cluster overlapping Turla and associated with FSB Centre 16.
actor_context.europe_relevance: Public reporting covers activity against Ukraine and European diplomatic and government targets.

actor_context.name: UNC1151
actor_context.summary: Belarus-linked intrusion cluster associated with credential theft and account compromise.
actor_context.europe_relevance: The reviewed record concerns government, political, media and civil-society targeting in Central and Eastern Europe.

actor_context.name: Mustang Panda
actor_context.summary: China-aligned espionage actor using spearphishing and removable-media operations.
actor_context.europe_relevance: Reviewed reporting includes diplomatic, government and maritime organisations in Europe.

actor_context.name: TA829 / RomCom
actor_context.summary: Russia-aligned hybrid cybercrime and espionage cluster using phishing, trojanised software and rapid exploitation.
actor_context.europe_relevance: The reviewed dossier covers European government, defence, energy, logistics and industrial targeting.

actor_context.name: LockBit
actor_context.summary: Ransomware-as-a-service ecosystem whose administrators supplied malware and infrastructure to affiliates.
actor_context.europe_relevance: Official disruption reporting documents extensive European victimisation, but affiliate activity is not one centrally attributed campaign.

actor_context.name: CL0P
actor_context.summary: Extortion and ransomware brand associated with mass exploitation of managed file-transfer and enterprise applications.
actor_context.europe_relevance: Reviewed campaigns affected organisations across Europe and beyond.

actor_context.name: Evil Corp
actor_context.summary: Russian cybercriminal organisation linked by authorities to Dridex-enabled theft and ransomware operations.
actor_context.europe_relevance: The public record includes extensive harm in the United Kingdom and Europe.

actor_context.name: Scattered Spider
actor_context.summary: Loose English-speaking cybercriminal collective known for help-desk social engineering, identity compromise and data theft.
actor_context.europe_relevance: The reviewed dossier includes the 2024 Transport for London intrusion; unrelated European incidents are not silently attributed to the group.

actor_context.name: Black Basta
actor_context.summary: Ransomware-as-a-service operation active since 2022 and associated with hundreds of affected organisations.
actor_context.europe_relevance: Joint government reporting documents affected organisations across Europe, North America and Australia.

actor_context.name: Z-Pentest
actor_context.summary: State-aligned pro-Russia hacktivist group associated with opportunistic operational-technology access.
actor_context.europe_relevance: Danish intelligence attributed a destructive 2024 water-utility incident to the group.
